rows.q: My credit card issuer charged me a late payment fee on 2019-05-01; it was my first late payment. What is the maximum safe-harbor late fee?
rows.answer: For a first late payment in 2019, the maximum safe-harbor late fee was $28 [1]. Under Regulation Z, these safe-harbor amounts are subject to annual inflation adjustments [2][1]. While major issuers often contract at or near the current safe-harbor limit, issuers are permitted to charge fees that are reasonable and proportional even if they differ from these specific safe-harbor thresholds [3][1].

rows.q: What was the maximum civil penalty per violation the FTC could seek under section 5(l) of the FTC Act on 2023-03-01?
rows.answer: On March 1, 2023, the maximum civil penalty the FTC could seek per violation under Section 5(l) of the FTC Act was $50,120 [1]. This amount became effective on January 11, 2023, following an inflation adjustment mandated by the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act Improvements Act of 2015 [1][2].

rows.q: What was the maximum civil penalty under section 5(m)(1)(A) of the FTC Act on 2024-03-01?
rows.answer: On March 1, 2024, the maximum civil penalty under section 5(m)(1)(A) of the FTC Act was $51,744 [1][2]. This amount became effective on January 10, 2024, following an annual inflation adjustment [1][3].
